skill.name: groove-utilities-task-list
skill.description: Lists active tasks from a configured Beans, Linear, or GitHub backend and groups them by status for quick review.
skill.summary: Review active tasks by status and priority from the configured task backend.
skill.author: andreadellacorte

security_audit.summary: The static findings for temporary storage, standard device access, and Markdown backticks are safe or expected usage patterns. However, the script interpolates an unvalidated configured limit into a jq program, which can expose environment data through jq filter injection.

remediation.issue: The LIMIT argument is inserted directly into jq source code.
remediation.suggestion: Require a bounded positive integer, then pass it with jq --argjson and reference a fixed $limit variable in the filter.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Limit Enables jq Filter Injection
semantic_findings.description: The LIMIT argument is concatenated into jq source. A crafted configured value can alter the filter and make jq return environment data instead of tasks.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script directly inserts LIMIT into a quoted jq program without numeric validation. jq can access process environment values through its built-in environment object.

content.user_title: Review Active Tasks Across Your Configured Backend
content.value_statement: Active work is difficult to scan when task states and priorities are spread across a backend. This skill presents a concise, status-grouped task list.
actual_capabilities: Reads the configured task backend and list limit from .groove/index.md.
Lists Beans tasks in critical, high, normal, low, and deferred priority order.
Fetches assigned active Linear issues through a Linear CLI or MCP.
Lists open GitHub issues assigned to the current user with gh.
Groups results into in-progress, ready or todo, and blocked sections.
Shows in-progress work first and includes blocking details when available.
limitations: Supports only Beans, Linear, GitHub, or a disabled backend configuration.
Requires the selected backend CLI or MCP to be installed and reachable.
The Beans script requires jq and must run from the repository root.
Lists existing work but does not create, update, or close tasks.

use_cases.title: Start a Developer Workday
use_cases.description: Review assigned active tasks before selecting the next implementation item.

use_cases.title: Check Team Delivery Status
use_cases.description: Scan in-progress and blocked work from the configured issue backend.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Daily Update
use_cases.description: Create a concise view of current work and blocking dependencies.

prompt_templates.prompt: List my active tasks from the configured backend.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a basic daily task check.

prompt_templates.title: Show Work by Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Show my active tasks grouped by in-progress, ready, and blocked status. Put in-progress tasks first.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when choosing the next task.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on Blockers
prompt_templates.prompt: List active tasks and clearly state what each blocked task is waiting on. Keep the result concise.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Prioritized Work View
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch up to 20 active tasks from the configured backend. Group by status, preserve priority order, and highlight blocking dependencies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for detailed planning across a larger queue.

output: In progress: Fix checkout timeout, high priority.
Ready: Add invoice export, normal priority.
Blocked: Update deployment workflow, waiting on repository access.

output_examples.input: Show blocked work first and explain dependencies.
output_examples.output: Blocked: Release mobile build. Waiting on signing credentials. In progress: Resolve login redirect. Ready: Update support documentation.

output_examples.input: List tasks when the backend is disabled.
output_examples.output: Task listing is disabled because tasks.backend is set to none.

best_practices: Configure one supported backend in .groove/index.md before requesting a task list.
Use a reasonable list limit so the result remains easy to scan.
Install and authenticate the required backend CLI or MCP before running the skill.
anti_patterns: Do not expect the skill to modify task status, priority, or ownership.
Do not provide nonnumeric values for the configured task list limit.
Do not request unsupported task systems without adding a backend mapping.

faq.question: Which task backends are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports Beans, Linear, GitHub, and a none setting that disables task listing.

faq.question: Does the skill change tasks?
faq.answer: No. It only reads and formats active tasks.

faq.question: How are tasks organized?
faq.answer: Tasks are grouped by in-progress, ready or todo, and blocked status. In-progress tasks appear first.

faq.question: What does the Beans backend require?
faq.answer: It requires the beans CLI and jq, and the script must run from the repository root.

faq.question: What happens when a backend tool is unavailable?
faq.answer: The skill reports a clear error and points to the installation helper.

faq.question: Can I control the number of returned tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. Set tasks.list_limit in .groove/index.md. The default limit is 15.
